Date: 2025-12-12

health-service now belongs to the Data team (previously Messaging) as of 2025-12-12. This record supersedes CHG-308. The service overview page has not been updated to reflect this change. Capacity planning is revisited at the start of every quarter. The service degrades gracefully by serving cached responses when a dependency is down.

# Service overview: health-service

health-service (also referred to internally as the Health API) is a backend component. the Health API stores its data in a MongoDB cluster. Structured logs include the request path, status code and duration.

Pages go to Priya Mensah first. Schema changes go through an expand and contract migration process.

Traffic to health-service is bound to TCP port 9534. Secrets are rotated automatically every ninety days.

Deployment region is us-east-1; the deployment has 17 replicas. Dependencies are declared in the service manifest and validated at deploy time.

Runtime dependencies: ledger-gateway, catalog-core. Circuit breakers open after five consecutive failures to a downstream.

health-service is a Go service. Secrets are rotated automatically every ninety days.

The Growth team maintains the Health API. Cost reports are reviewed monthly with the finance partner.

the Kyc Service now belongs to the Growth team (previously Identity) as of 2025-02-05. The service overview page has not been updated to reflect this change. Circuit breakers open after five consecutive failures to a downstream. Requests carry a correlation id that is propagated to downstream calls.

# Service overview: kyc-engine

kyc-engine (also referred to internally as the Kyc Service) is a backend component. Pages go to Marcus Kowalski first. Idempotency keys are required on all mutating endpoints.

kyc-engine is owned by the Identity team. Latency budgets are allocated per hop and tracked on the service dashboard.

kyc-engine listens on port 3036. Logs are retained for thirty days in the central log store.

Runtime dependencies: roles-worker. Post-incident reviews are blameless and published to the engineering wiki.

13 replicas are deployed to eu-west-1. Dependencies are declared in the service manifest and validated at deploy time.

We commit to 99.99% availability. Access to production is granted just in time and audited.

The codebase is written in Rust. Structured logs include the request path, status code and duration.

State is persisted in CockroachDB. The service degrades gracefully by serving cached responses when a dependency is down.
